name: OpenAIAgent
title: OpenAI Agent
description: Multi-turn agent that works through a problem using MCP tools
whenToUse: Reach for this when a step needs the model to work through a problem using tools rather than answer in one pass: look something up, act on what it found, then decide what to do next. A single prompt with no tool use is cheaper and more predictable done elsewhere. Attach MCP provider nodes by service edge to give it capabilities.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Data from previous nodes that can be referenced in templates

outputs.name: thinking
outputs.description: Short customer-safe status lines, emitted in real time

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Streaming text response, emitted in real time

outputs.name: reasoning
outputs.description: The model's own reasoning summary (not the narrator's status line)

maxTurns.title: Max Turns
maxTurns.description: How many times the model may go round the tool loop. 1 answers in a single pass and never calls a tool. 5 to 10 suits an agent that looks things up and acts on what it finds. Higher costs more and takes longer.

reasoningSummary.title: Reasoning Summary
reasoningSummary.description: Summaries must be requested or the API emits no reasoning events at all.

systemPrompt.title: System Prompt
systemPrompt.description: Standing instructions for the agent: its role, how to work, when to use its tools. Optional. Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.reactAgent}}.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: The task to work on. Usually wired in from an upstream node.

enableUserMemory.title: User Memory
enableUserMemory.description: Remember the user across conversations — the agent saves what it learns and can look it up later.

enableAgentMemory.title: Agent Memory
enableAgentMemory.description: Give the agent a working notebook for long-running tasks — it tracks its goal, progress and next steps between runs.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.

package.name: openai
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# The package envelope, and now the ONLY envelope: this package is fully
# declarative. All five nodes are manifests, there is no src/ and no package.json,
# so nothing here is built, published or imported. The retired TypeScript sits at
# _legacy/nodes/openai for reference.
#
# A code node of the same type always beats a manifest at load, which is what made
# migrating one node at a time possible. With the code gone there is nothing left
# to beat these.

name: openai
displayName: OpenAI
description: OpenAI integration for Unoverse
version: 1.2.0
category: ai
# First-party. The marketplace shows this on every node the package registers, so
# "who am I trusting with this credential" is answerable without leaving the screen.
publisher: unoverse
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749262616/gravity/icons/ChatGPT-Logo.svg.webp

features:
  - GPT-5.6 models
  - Streaming responses
  - Function/tool calling
  - Text embeddings
  - Structured JSON output
  - Vision (image inputs)

# The ONLY hosts this package's nodes may call. The executor refuses anything else.
#
# A manifest cannot execute code, but without this it could still say "send this
# credential to evil.example", which is exfiltration with no code at all. One short
# reviewable list is what makes a manifest safe to accept from someone else.
allowedHosts:
  - api.openai.com

# Executor capabilities every manifest node here depends on. Deploy REFUSES this
# package if the target universe's executor cannot satisfy them, so a manifest can
# never name a capability that only exists on a newer executor.
requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [sse, json]
  executorVersion: ">=1.0.0"

credentials.openAICredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# The SHAPE of the credential, never its value. Transcribed from
# plugin-base/src/credentials/openai.ts, which this package re-exports today.
#
# Values live where they already live: encrypted in Postgres on a deployed universe,
# and in the developer's own .env locally. That is why a manifest is safe to commit.
#
# Nodes reference this by NAME. At run time context.credentials holds EVERY credential
# in the workflow keyed by name, and the executor must select by name, never by
# scanning for the first object with an apiKey: openAICredential, apolloCredential,
# hunterCredential and searchapiCredential all expose one, so a scan silently
# authenticates against the wrong service the moment a second is added to the
# workflow (04-credentials.md).

name: openAICredential
displayName: OpenAI
description: Credentials for OpenAI API
documentationUrl: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your OpenAI API key
    placeholder: sk-...

  - name: organizationId
    displayName: Organization ID
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Your OpenAI organization ID (optional)
    placeholder: org-...

  - name: baseUrl
    displayName: Base URL
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Custom API endpoint (optional)
    default: https://api.openai.com/v1

shared.endpoints.yaml:
# OpenAI's endpoints. Written once here rather than seven times across the nodes.
#
# No chat/completions: every node uses the Responses API. `messages` is the legacy shape.
#
#   url: { $ref: ../../shared/endpoints.yaml#/responses }

responses: https://api.openai.com/v1/responses
embeddings: https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings
shared.models.yaml:
# The canonical GPT model list, the SINGLE source every OpenAI node references,
# organised by TIER. Transcribed from src/shared/models.ts.
#
# Models come in three tiers. A new generation is a one-line edit per tier here, and
# every node plus every saved workflow moves over automatically.
#
# The DATA lives here. The FALLBACK LOGIC (resolveModel: a retired id resolves to the
# current best model in its tier, so replacing a generation cannot break a saved
# workflow) is computation, not description, so it belongs to the executor. It is
# declared per config field as `resolver: modelTier`, not written here.

# One current model per tier. Update these three lines when a new generation ships.
byTier:
  small: gpt-5.6-luna # cost-optimized, high-volume
  medium: gpt-5.6-terra # balanced intelligence/cost, the default
  large: gpt-5.6 # frontier, complex work

# Balanced middle tier, the sensible default for most work.
default: gpt-5.6-terra

# The NARRATOR: the model that writes an agent's short "thinking" status line. A separate
# concern from the model doing the work, so it is named separately.
#
# Deliberately NOT the 5.6 family: 5.6 is luna/sol/terra with no nano tier, and this call
# exists to reach the user fast, not to be clever. Measured 2026-07-26, three runs each,
# same prompt and schema:
#
#   gpt-5.4-nano   avg 1137ms   [1470, 905, 1035]
#   gpt-5.6-luna   avg 2043ms   [1846, 2337, 1945]
#
# Luna is ~80% slower and less consistent for lines that are indistinguishable in quality.
# Re-measure when a faster small model ships; never assume.
narrator: gpt-5.4-nano


# The picker's options. Listed large first so the strongest reads first.
enum:
  - gpt-5.6
  - gpt-5.6-terra
  - gpt-5.6-luna

enumNames:
  - Sol (Frontier, complex work)
  - Terra (Balanced intelligence/cost)
  - Luna (Cost-optimized, high-volume)
shared.tools.yaml:
# The OpenAI Responses tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does NOT belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it
# does not belong copied into every node either. It belongs here: shared by every OpenAI
# node, imported whole.
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#     maxTurns: 5            # local keys layer on top and win
#
# When OpenAI changes how a function call is expressed, exactly one file changes.
# NO SDK. This is the wire format, described as data.

# How ONE tool is offered to the model. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }
toolsInto: tools

# How a call ARRIVES in the stream.
call:
  match: response.output_item.done
  when: "return response.item.type === 'function_call'"
  id: "return response.item.call_id"
  name: "return response.item.name"
  arguments: "return response.item.arguments"

# How ONE result goes BACK. `call` is { id, name, output }.
result: >-
  return { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output }
resultsInto: input

# Always auto: which tool to reach for is carried by the tool DESCRIPTIONS, never by
# forcing a choice.
choiceInto: tool_choice
choice: auto

# How a turn chains to the next without resending the transcript.
continuity:
  match: response.completed
  from: "return response.response.id"
  into: previous_response_id

files.api/events.yaml:
# EVERYTHING THAT LEAVES THIS NODE, one row per output connector, in the SAME ORDER the
# connectors are declared in interface.yaml. Read this and you know the node's whole
# outward behaviour without opening another file. Lint holds the order.
#
# `from` says where a row fires:
#   response   an event on the main SSE stream, matched by type
#   narrator   a line from the cheap side model
#   tool       after a tool call RETURNS, with its result
#   complete   once, at the end

# The customer-safe status line, written FOR the customer by the narrator. Not the
# model's own thinking, which is `reasoning` below and is not safe to show.
- emit: thinking
  from: narrator
  value: "return narrator.line"

# Accumulated, not the fragment: a consumer wants the answer so far, not one word. And
# throttled, or a long answer becomes hundreds of events. Nothing held back is lost; it
# is flushed when the run ends.
- emit: stream
  from: response
  match: response.output_text.delta
  value: "return response.delta"
  accumulate: true
  throttleMs: 200

# The MODEL's own reasoning summary. Only produced when reasoningEffort is above none
# AND a reasoningSummary is requested; the API sends nothing otherwise.
- emit: reasoning
  from: response
  match: response.reasoning_summary_text.delta
  value: "return response.delta"
  accumulate: true
  throttleChars: 150

# The tool RESULT. It is never in the HTTP stream: our tool loop produced it, which is
# why this cannot be a `from: response` row. Emitting the tool CALL here instead was a
# real bug, since it fired before the tool had run and carried the model's raw arguments.
- emit: mcpResult
  from: tool
  value: "return { name: call.name, result: call.output }"

# The settled answer: the last accumulated value the stream reached. `at(-1)` and
  # not `pop()`: the expression sandbox allows no mutating method, by design.
- emit: text
  from: complete
  value: "return events.filter(e => e.emit === 'stream').map(e => e.value).at(-1) ?? ''"
files.api/narrate.yaml:
# The narrator: the `thinking` line, written by a second and much cheaper model in THIS
# agent's voice. Deliberately not shared, because the copy is tuned for this node.
#
# Not to be confused with `reasoning` in events.yaml, which is the MAIN model's own
# summary. The platform contributes only timing: a local line at 0ms because the round
# trip has a ~1s floor and the main model's first token beats it, never awaited, fall
# back on any failure, and drop late lines.
#
# Which connector its line lands on is NOT here: that is the `from: narrator` row in
# events.yaml, like every other thing that leaves this node.

instant:
  - Let me look into this for you...
  - Okay, one moment while I check...
  - Let me see how I can help...
  - Just a second while I look at this...
  - Checking the best way to help you...

fallback: Checking the best next step...

request:
  method: POST
  url: { $ref: endpoints#responses }
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.openAICredential.apiKey }}"
  timeoutMs: 8000
  transport: json
  body:
    # NOT the model doing the work: this line has to beat the main stream, so it wants
    # the fastest small model there is. Named in shared/models.yaml with the timings
    # behind the choice, so every agent moves together when a faster one ships.
    model: { $ref: models#narrator }
    max_output_tokens: 600
    instructions: |-
      You are writing the short status line a virtual assistant shows the customer while it prepares its reply — the visible "thinking" line above the answer.

      The line must:
      - Be one sentence only, 6–12 words.
      - Sound like the assistant getting on with the task: what it is checking, confirming, or looking into.
      - Use natural, warm, present-tense assistant voice.
      - NEVER be commentary about the customer's message itself (never "what X refers to", "the message says", "you mentioned").
      - NEVER quote or repeat the customer's words.
      - NEVER repeat abbreviations, acronyms, brand names, or product names from the message.
      - Avoid assumptions about the customer's goal, preference, eligibility, or situation.
      - Avoid phrases like "the message is brief", "I asked", "I need to understand", or "before answering".
      - No private chain-of-thought, no step-by-step reasoning.
      - Never mention tool, system, or service names.
      - No label such as "Reasoning summary:".

      Good examples:
      - Okay, let me check the right support route.
      - Let me clarify what help you need today.
      - I'll confirm the relevant options for your request.
      - Checking the best next step for this query.
      - Let me review the available support options.
      - I'll check the right process to follow.

      Bad examples:
      - Confirming what "hello" refers to for your query.
      - The message is very brief, so I asked a few questions.
      - I am reasoning about what the user might want.
      - The user may be looking for a course or qualification.
      - I need to infer their goal before answering.
      - Reasoning summary: I checked the available options.
    # WHAT THE NARRATOR IS TOLD about this moment. Two moments, two framings, chosen with
    # an ordinary {{#if}} over the {{event.*}} root, exactly like any other template value
    # in any other manifest field. Nothing here is special.
    input: |-
      {{#if (eq event.kind "turnStart")}}
      For topical context only (do NOT quote or reference it), the message from the customer was: """{{event.userMessage}}""". Write the status line the assistant shows while preparing its reply.
      {{else}}
      The assistant is now looking something up for the customer using an internal capability named "{{event.toolName}}"{{#if event.args}} with input {{toJSON event.args}}{{/if}}. Write the thinking line describing what is being checked or done (never name the capability).
      {{/if}}
    text:
      format:
        type: json_schema
        name: thinking
        strict: true
        schema:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [line]
          properties:
            line: { type: string }

response:
  line: >-
    return JSON.parse(
      response.output.filter(o => o.type === 'message')
        .flatMap(o => o.content).filter(c => c.type === 'output_text')
        .map(c => c.text).join('') || '{}'
    ).line
files.api/run.yaml:
# The main call: OpenAI's Responses API. NO SDK.
#
# The Agents SDK is client-side orchestration over this same endpoint, so what it gives
# you is a loop, not a capability. Doing the loop from here keeps an agent portable: the
# platform counts turns and spots a stuck one, and everything about OpenAI's wire format
# lives in this folder.
#
# A CALL is one thing: how it is made AND how its reply is framed. That is why transport,
# terminator and error live here and not in a file of their own.

- name: generate
  method: POST
  url: { $ref: endpoints#responses }

  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.openAICredential.apiKey }}"

  body:
    model: "{{ config.model }}"
    input: "{{ config.prompt }}"
    instructions: "{{ config.systemPrompt }}"
    max_output_tokens: "{{ config.maxTokens }}"
    stream: true
    reasoning:
      effort: "{{ config.reasoningEffort }}"
      summary: "{{ config.reasoningSummary }}"
    text:
      verbosity: "{{ config.verbosity }}"

  timeoutMs: 600000

  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    # 520/522/524 are CLOUDFLARE EDGE errors, not OpenAI ones: the origin returned something the
    # edge could not read, never answered, or exceeded the edge timeout. They are transient in exactly
    # the way 502/503/504 are, and a live run hit a 520 after 154s with no retry because they were
    # missing here. Added alongside the origin 5xx rather than instead of them.
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 520, 522, 524]

  # How the reply is framed.
  transport: sse
  terminator: "[DONE]"

  # A 200 carrying an error body must not read as success.
  error:
    when: "return response.type === 'response.failed'"
    message: "return response.response.error.message"
files.api/toolExchange.yaml:
# The tool loop's protocol, described HERE and not in the platform. The runtime only
# counts turns, spots a stuck loop, and mints what discovery unlocks.

# OpenAI's tool protocol, imported whole. Local keys below layer on top.
$ref: tools

# The dial. 1 answers in a single pass and cannot use a tool at all; higher makes it
# work through a problem.
maxTurns: "{{ config.maxTurns }}"
# The SAME call with the SAME arguments three times is stuck. maxTurns does not catch
# it: a model calling many DIFFERENT tools forever is not stuck by that rule.
stuckAfterRepeats: 3
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  # `prompt` IS REQUIRED, for the reason spelled out in OpenAI/config.yaml: this node's body builds
  # the Responses API's required `input` from `prompt` alone, and `resolveBody` omits a key that
  # resolved to "" — so an empty prompt drops the field and the vendor answers
  # `400 Missing required parameter: 'input'` rather than anything a reader could act on.
  required: [model, maxTurns, prompt]

  properties:
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      enum: { $ref: models#enum }
      enumNames: { $ref: models#enumNames }
      default: { $ref: models#default }
      resolve: modelTier

    # THE DIAL THAT MAKES THIS AN AGENT.
    #
    # One turn is one model call. A tool call costs another, because the result has to go
    # back for the model to use it. So maxTurns: 1 is a one-shot generator that cannot use
    # tools at all, and anything above it is an agent working through a problem.
    #
    # That is the only real difference between this and a streaming text node, which is
    # why they are one node with a dial rather than two nodes.
    maxTurns:
      type: number
      title: Max Turns
      description: >-
        How many times the model may go round the tool loop. 1 answers in a single pass
        and never calls a tool. 5 to 10 suits an agent that looks things up and acts on
        what it finds. Higher costs more and takes longer.
      default: 10
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 30

    reasoningEffort:
      type: string
      title: Reasoning Effort
      enum: [none, low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
      default: medium

    reasoningSummary:
      type: string
      title: Reasoning Summary
      description: Summaries must be requested or the API emits no reasoning events at all.
      enum: [auto, concise, detailed]
      default: concise

    verbosity:
      type: string
      title: Verbosity
      enum: [low, medium, high]
      default: medium

    systemPrompt:
      type: string
      title: System Prompt
      description: >-
        Standing instructions for the agent: its role, how to work, when to use its tools.
        Optional. Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.reactAgent}}.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    prompt:
      type: string
      title: Prompt
      description: The task to work on. Usually wired in from an upstream node.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    maxTokens:
      type: number
      title: Max Output Tokens
      default: 4096
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 128000

    # THE MEMORY TOGGLES, transcribed from the retired node — they vanished in the migration
    # and the whole memory system sat idle because nothing declared them (found live
    # 2026-07-30: healthy memory server, empty ingest stream). Three consumers key off
    # these flags, and none is this manifest's business to implement:
    #   - the ENGINE injects the goal-memory toolset from `enableAgentMemory`
    #     (PlatformMemoryCore reads the node's config — no node-side code, ever)
    #   - the EXECUTOR hydrates the prompt with the user's context snapshot before the run
    #   - the EXECUTOR ingests each completed turn to the memory server after it
    enableUserMemory:
      type: boolean
      title: User Memory
      description: >-
        Remember the user across conversations — the agent saves what it learns and can look
        it up later.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    enableAgentMemory:
      type: boolean
      title: Agent Memory
      description: >-
        Give the agent a working notebook for long-running tasks — it tracks its goal,
        progress and next steps between runs.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

ui:order:
  [authRequired, authRole, model, maxTurns, reasoningEffort, reasoningSummary, verbosity, systemPrompt, prompt, maxTokens, enableUserMemory, enableAgentMemory]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes that can be referenced in templates

outputs:
  # The NARRATOR's line, not the model's. `reasoning` below is the model's own summary;
  # this is the short customer-safe status written by a separate cheap model.
  - name: thinking
    type: string
    description: Short customer-safe status lines, emitted in real time

  - name: stream
    type: object
    description: Streaming text response, emitted in real time

  - name: reasoning
    type: string
    description: The model's own reasoning summary (not the narrator's status line)

  - name: mcpResult
    type: object
    description: MCP tool results

  - name: text
    type: string
    description: The complete generated text (final output)

credentials:
  - name: openAICredential
    required: true
    displayName: OpenAI API

serviceConnectors:
  # Attach MCP provider nodes here to give the agent capabilities. Nothing wired means
  # no tools, and it degrades to a single request rather than failing.
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: false
    description: MCP service connector, automatic schema discovery
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

# The agent, as a manifest. Responses API + the tool loop. NO SDK.
#
# NOT AT PARITY with the retired TypeScript agent in ONE respect: no cross-execution
# conversation. Memory (both toggles + lanes) restored 2026-07-30; the narrator IS here
# (api/narrate.yaml). See the gap note at the bottom.
#
# It takes the real type, because a type is the identity a saved graph stores and an
# invented suffix would put an implementation detail on a name people read. There is no
# TypeScript registration left to compete with it; the retired code is kept for
# reference at _legacy/nodes/openai.

type: OpenAIAgent
kind: CallbackNode

name: OpenAI Agent
category: AI
color: "#2F6F66"

description: Multi-turn agent that works through a problem using MCP tools

# The wiring sentence used to sit in the MIDDLE. Doc 14: mechanism last, always, because
# opening or interrupting with plumbing vocabulary drags the embedding towards wiring
# concepts and away from the job a planner's task query actually describes.
whenToUse: >-
  Reach for this when a step needs the model to work through a problem using tools rather
  than answer in one pass: look something up, act on what it found, then decide what to do
  next. A single prompt with no tool use is cheaper and more predictable done elsewhere.
  Attach MCP provider nodes by service edge to give it capabilities.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable: an agent turn is non-deterministic and reaches the outside world
  # through its tools. Reusing a prior answer would skip real side effects.
  cacheable: false

# ── NOT AT PARITY with the TypeScript OpenAIAgent. One gap left: ─────────────────────
#
#   conversation  Redis-backed previous_response_id ACROSS executions, keyed by
#                 conversationId, plus the "reset conversation" phrase. Multi-turn works
#                 WITHIN one execution here; it does not survive between them.
#
# memory CLOSED 2026-07-30: the toggles are back in config.yaml and the two lanes
# (hydratePromptWithUserMemory before the run, ingestConversationTurn after) run in the
# EXECUTOR off those flags (executor/memory.ts) — the same generic wiring the engine uses
# to inject the goal-memory toolset from enableAgentMemory. This file declares only the
# toggles; any agent manifest that declares them gets the lanes.
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# No MCP provider is wired on the bench, so this exercises the one-shot path
# (maxTurns still bounds it; with no tools the loop degrades to a single request).
# The tool loop itself is proven separately against a stub bridge.
testData:
  config:
    model: gpt-5.6
    maxTurns: 5
    reasoningEffort: none
    reasoningSummary: concise
    verbosity: low
    systemPrompt: You are a concise research assistant.
    prompt: Name the three states of matter, comma separated.
    maxTokens: 300

  inputs:
    signal:
      topic: states of matter

  expect:
    text: "return output.text.length > 0"
